ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
The total mass of a hot air balloon, researchers, and all equipment is $M = 900\mathrm{kg}$. After hovering at an altitude of $400\mathrm{m}$, due to a malfunction, the buoyant force acting on the balloon decreases. The researchers measure that the balloon's vertical downward velocity increases by $6\mathrm{m/s}$ in $3\mathrm{s}$. If the maximum safe landing speed of the balloon is $4\mathrm{m/s}$, in order to land the balloon safely, the researchers jettison an object of mass $m=300\mathrm{kg}$, causing the balloon to undergo uniform decelerated motion vertically downward.  Neglecting air resistance on the balloon and the change in balloon velocity during the jettison, and assuming the buoyant force remains constant during the balloon's motion, and the gravitational acceleration is $g=10\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$.

1. Determine the minimum altitude of the balloon above the ground when the object is jettisoned.

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: The total mass of a hot air balloon, researchers, and all equipment is $M = 900\mathrm{kg}$. After hovering at an altitude of $400\mathrm{m}$, due to a malfunction, the buoyant force acting on the balloon decreases. The researchers measure that the balloon's vertical downward velocity increases by $6\mathrm{m/s}$ in $3\mathrm{s}$. If the maximum safe landing speed of the balloon is $4\mathrm{m/s}$, in order to land the balloon safely, the researchers jettison an object of mass $m=300\mathrm{kg}$, causing the balloon to undergo uniform decelerated motion vertically downward. Neglecting air resistance on the balloon and the change in balloon velocity during the jettison, and assuming the buoyant force remains constant during the balloon's motion, and the gravitational acceleration is $g=10\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$. 1. Determine the minimum altitude of the balloon above the ground when the object is jettisoned.
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Take downward as the positive direction. The measured velocity increase before jettison is 6 m/s in 3 s, so the downward acceleration is a1 = 6/3 = 2 m/s^2. Before jettison, the mass is M = 900 kg, so Mg - F_b = M a1. Thus F_b = Mg - M a1 = 900×10 - 900×2 = 7200 N. After jettisoning 300 kg, the remaining mass is 600 kg. The net force in the downward-positive direction is 600g - F_b = 6000 - 7200 = -1200 N, so the acceleration after jettison is a2 = -1200/600 = -2 m/s^2, i.e. uniform deceleration while moving downward. If the object is jettisoned at altitude h, then before jettison the balloon has descended 400 - h from rest under acceleration a1, so v_j^2 = 2a1(400 - h) = 4(400 - h). For the limiting safe landing condition, the landing speed is 4 m/s after descending distance h with acceleration a2 = -2 m/s^2: 4^2 = v_j^2 + 2a2h = v_j^2 - 4h. Substitute v_j^2 = 4(400 - h): 16 = 4(400 - h) - 4h = 1600 - 8h. Therefore h = (1600 - 16)/8 = 198 m.
